practice_questions.text: Read this poem and write a response to Part (i) in 16 minutes. How does the poet use language and structure to present their feelings?
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (13–15) 3 focused paragraphs. Thematic statement. Language + structure analysed. Effects explained.

Lower bands: progressively less analysis and less evidence.

practice_questions.text: Now compare both poems in 35 minutes. How does the poet of Poem 2 also present [theme]?
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (21–25) 2 paragraphs. Sustained comparison. Both poems referenced in every sentence.

Lower bands: progressively less analysis and less evidence.

practice_questions.text: Practise annotating this poem in 4 minutes. Identify: the most striking image, the key structural feature, and the overall tone.
practice_questions.marks: This is an annotation exercise. Check: did you identify specific quotations? Did you note techniques? Did you identify the theme?

practice_questions.text: Write a response to Part (i) focusing on only 3 quotations, analysed in depth.
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (13–15) 3 quotations, each with detailed connotation and effect analysis. Depth over quantity.

Lower bands: progressively less analysis and less evidence.

practice_questions.text: Write a comparison response using the framework: opening, 2 comparison paragraphs, closing.
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (21–25) Clear framework followed. Sustained comparison. Comparative connectives used.

Lower bands: progressively less analysis and less evidence.

practice_questions.text: Read this poem you find difficult. Focus only on tone and word choice. Write a response.
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (13–15) Identifies tone. Analyses word choices that create it. Offers personal interpretation even without full understanding.

Lower bands: progressively less analysis and less evidence.
